summary: Final increment for this window, kept honest and low-risk. The narrowed precondition of the snapshot-boundary loop points at a practical trigger I have not executed: a snapshot taken while the leader's applied index lags the log end by at least TrailingLogs. I attempted that variant locally (a 15 ms-per-apply FSM behind a small SnapshotThreshold/Interval with TrailingLogs=2 and a wide uncommitted suffix on the peer), but the harness never reached its precondition — no leader snapshot index was ever observed — so I recorded it as a necessary gap with a concrete discriminator instead of shipping an experiment that would fail. The update registers investigation @q-practical-trigger with the hypothesis (taking a snapshot at index L while the log end is at least TrailingLogs ahead makes compactLogsWithTrailing delete up to L, so the retained log begins above L and the peer's stale entry at L can only be reconciled by repeated whole-snapshot transfers), a gap describing what the harness must establish explicitly (drive applies faster than the FSM drains, or snapshot during a known backlog), and an unresolved interpretation that claims no measurement: the failed attempt is reported as a failed harness that neither supports nor refutes the positive direction. The asserted results stay scoped exactly as before — TrailingLogs=0 with a snapshot taken at the log end, evidenced by the single-peer witness CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7, the sealed-partition witness CheckRun f66fa4e4e0514f7e95b7788032144a30, and the cause-isolating control CheckRun beca431464bf44ab9c3354145c21899f — with the caveat that TrailingLogs=0 must remain explicit in the scope until the backlog variant is executed. The draft harness in the workspace is unchanged from the three-case version the controller already executed, so nothing broken is registered. Structural validation returned valid=true.
